name: Mooney 301

useful: design figure: 4,000 gross less 2,548 empty (Air International Airdata File, Jan 1984), not stated as weighed; Mooney's spec sheet claims 1,600

259 mph cruise, Jane's 1983-84 pp. 444-445 (via Wikipedia); conditions not stated; also a design-era figure

why_died_short: LTV takeover forced Mooney's sale; new owners wanted 300 kt; became the TBM 700
why_died: Republic Steel's takeover by LTV forced the sale of Mooney. The prototype was about 200 lb over its projected weight and, with aero work unfinished, slower than desired; the new French-led owners wanted close to 300 kt, which needed a turbine, and moved the effort into the Socata joint venture that became the TBM 700 (Mooney Events; Plane & Pilot; docs/rights/mooney-301.md).
rights: No TC; one prototype, scrapped. M30 data went to Socata in 1987; whether Mooney International or Daher holds it is not shown (docs/rights/mooney-301.md).
safety: No accidents found.
useful_asflown: AERO lower-bound estimate: 1,452 less the prototype's ~200 lb weight overrun (Mooney Events; Wikipedia; docs/rights/mooney-301.md). If 2,548 lb already includes the overrun, ~1,400 (1,600 less 200). Never weighed in public record
flags: useful load and cruise are design figures; the only prototype was ~200 lb over projected weight and 'slower than desired', and no as-flown speed or weight is published (Mooney Events; docs/rights/mooney-301.md)
the published 986 nm range is a 45 min reserve figure; fuel and flow give 1,016 nm on that basis, consistent within 3%

1,000 nm plus 45 min at 235 kt and 19.7 gph needs 98.6 of 100 gal with no climb allowance; below 231 KTAS at the same flow (about 4 kt under the design figure) it cannot carry the reserve (at Jane's 225 kt it needs 102 gal)

235 KTAS at 270 hp, 25,000 ft, 4,000 lb implies CD0 ~0.019 (AR 9.0, e 0.80, prop eta 0.80; AERO, grade E), optimistic for a 1983 pressurized single; at CD0 +20% the same power gives ~220 KTAS, still a pass on speed
